# David Packer Recommends Weighted Pull-Ups At About 50 Of Your Body Weight As A Front Lever Prerequisite

David Packer recommends aiming for weighted pull-ups at about 50 of your body weight for about three to five reps as a prerequisite to achieve a front lever for two seconds. [src: vid-lkcLJc2c0NQ]

## Details

- If you are 75 kilograms, doing 40 kilogram weighted pull-ups for about three to five reps can almost guarantee a front lever for two seconds even if your hips are sagging. [src: vid-lkcLJc2c0NQ]
- David Packer coached like maybe 10 people who did not have a front lever, got the 40 kg pull-ups for reps, and then had their front lever for a few seconds. [src: vid-lkcLJc2c0NQ]

## Evidence

- vid-lkcLJc2c0NQ (David Packer): "go for weighted pull-ups aim for about 50 of your body weight and shoot for about five reps so if you're say 75 kilograms if you can if you can do 40 kilogram weighted pull-ups for about three to five reps i i can almost guarantee you can do a front lever for two seconds"
- vid-lkcLJc2c0NQ (David Packer): "even if your hips are sagging a bit you have enough strength to do it straight away because i've coached like maybe 10 that did not have a front lever bang got the 40 kg pull-ups for reps and they had their front lever for a few seconds"

## Why This Matters

David Packer says that after you have that front lever for two seconds from the pull-up base, then you start doing the raises front lever to inverted hang. [src: vid-lkcLJc2c0NQ]
